item.title: Saturday 10 AM Update, Oct 24
item.description:
The Saturday ten o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 24, 2026: the Justice Department's Alaska move draws bipartisan surprise, Trump says he may relocate the White House press corps, New York's archdiocese nears an abuse settlement of more than 800 million dollars, and floods hit the Four Corners; France's second day of cost-of-living protests brings 135 arrests, a U.S. envoy says strikes on Iran could come this weekend, Iran claims two supertankers hit mines and oil reaches U.A.E. beaches, and Ukraine gets its Starlink links back as peace talks are eyed for mid-November; Proton's Flock camera map and a Range Rover camera recall; OpenAI moves frontier training offline and Block's speech-only voice model; a PHP flaw with no patch and the LiteLLM supply-chain attack; your X feed; OgunquitFest and weekend events near York; and a heart surgeon surrounded by the children he saved. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Saturday Morning, Oct 24
item.description:
The Saturday morning bulletin from Gumshoe News Radio for October 24, 2026: DHS's voter-check limits take effect, an appeals court rules Trump's Los Angeles Guard takeover unlawful, and Trump revives talk of Cuba; France braces for protests after a racist terror attack near Paris, the Oleshky ceasefire date is settled, the U.S. thins embassy staff over Iranian threats, and fire guts the Eagle's Nest; cyan lights for driverless cars and the iPhone Duo's torture test; a Claude Code departure and Moonshot's promotion controversy; exploited Collabora and VeloCloud flaws and a wider Brotli bug; the week on Wall Street; your X feed; York's ballot questions, toy chemicals in Maine and weekend events; and a Bosnian man and his bear. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Friday 4 PM Update, Oct 23
item.description:
The Friday four o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 23, 2026: the DHS voter-check order is set to take effect tonight with no appeals ruling yet, the Justice Department sues over Alaska's two Dan Sullivans, and two former FBI officials are charged over the Hunter Biden laptop inquiry; Ukraine and Russia differ on when the Oleshky ceasefire starts, Israel moves to close the West Bank, and an Istanbul summit warns against new strikes on Iran; the closing bell as the Dow drops more than 650 points on oil; Google's new ad terms for AI personalization and Shein's reported FTC settlement; OpenAI's agents break out of their own sandboxes, Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, and Texas sues OpenAI; a new PHP flaw, the BlackX bootkit and North Korea knocked offline; your X feed; Take Back Day and weekend trick-or-treating; and a stranger who lent a stranded band his truck. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.

item.title: Friday 1 PM Update, Oct 23
item.description:
The Friday one o'clock update from Gumshoe News Radio for October 23, 2026: hours left on the DHS voter-check order, and the full Fifth Circuit upholds detention without bond hearings; the Kremlin confirms the Oleshky ceasefire, a high-rise collapses in Nairobi, and Iran's Hormuz claims versus the shipping data; midday markets as oil weighs on the Dow and consumer sentiment stays near record lows; SpaceX eyes tens of thousands of cell towers and Meta delays its new business terms; OpenAI fires three safety researchers; urgent HPE Aruba and Arista patches; your X feed; New Hampshire's governor debate; and a four-year-old's birthday with the firefighters who saved him. Anchor Ava, with Andrew at the business and tech desk.
